metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Proportion of incorrectly reported components (cells and nets not in the ground truth) out of all reported components.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.name: inference_latency

acceptance_criteria: The submitted trigger_cells array contains the exact instance names of the AOI21 and OAI22 cells that form the trigger.
The submitted trigger_nets array contains the exact name of the net connecting the AOI21 and OAI22 cells.
The submitted payload_cells array contains the exact instance name of the XOR cell driving control_out.
The submitted payload_nets array contains the exact name of the net connecting the trigger output to the XOR cell input.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Two labeled AOI/OAI cells jointly implement the rare state-and-input match; their output controls the labeled payload XOR on control_out.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the reported trigger cells include the specific AOI21 and OAI22 instances that implement the rare comparator, and if the reported trigger nets include the internal net connecting them.
security_requirements.requirement: The detection method must identify the trigger logic even when it is absorbed into complex AOI/OAI cells.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check if the reported payload cells include the XOR gate instance that drives control_out, and if the reported payload nets include the net connecting the trigger output to the XOR input.
security_requirements.requirement: The detection method must identify the payload logic that flips the control_out signal.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Technology mapping obscures the recognizable AND-tree shape used by structural Trojan detectors.

constraints: The netlist uses a small technology-mapped cell vocabulary including AOI21, OAI22, INV, XOR, and DFF.
The netlist is a flat, gate-level Verilog file.
The control_out signal is a single-bit output of the top-level module.
expected_outputs: A valid trojan_report.json file in the submission directory.
The report must list at least one trigger cell instance and at least one payload cell instance.
The report must list at least one trigger net and at least one payload net.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json must be valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The submitted trojan_report.json must contain the exact top-level keys: "trigger_cells", "trigger_nets", "payload_cells", "payload_nets".
Each of the four required keys must map to a non-empty array of strings.
All reported cell instance names and net names must exist in the provided netlist (design.v).

public_spec.interface: The participant must produce a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json. The file must contain a JSON object with the following required fields: "trigger_cells" (array of strings, instance names of cells implementing the trigger condition), "trigger_nets" (array of strings, names of nets carrying the trigger signal), "payload_cells" (array of strings, instance names of cells implementing the payload), "payload_nets" (array of strings, names of nets carrying the payload effect). All arrays must be non-empty. The evaluator will parse this file and compare its contents against the hidden ground truth.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist and identify any logic that could cause the control_out signal to flip under a specific, rare input condition. Report the instance names of the cells and nets involved in this behavior.
public_spec.response_format: A JSON object with keys "trigger_cells", "trigger_nets", "payload_cells", "payload_nets", each mapping to a non-empty array of strings.

title: Trigger absorbed into mapped AOI cells
